status: BLOCKED_BACKEND_QUALIFICATION; safe repair architecture and qualification route identified, no production fix claimed

observed_repo_guard.fact: The base deliberately returns ElevatedWindowsSandboxIsolationUnavailable before elevated provisioning, ACL edits and spawn; it also states that an original native four-cell deletion matrix found an ambient parent FILE_DELETE_CHILD escape even after narrowing restricting SIDs.

token_source.fact: Capability-only workspace token construction already omits WRITE_RESTRICTED and removes broad Everyone/logon restricting SIDs; dedicated-account token construction additionally retains the dedicated user SID for owner-scoped named pipes. Token construction success alone does not qualify child launch/read/IPC or deletion containment.

primary_sources.support: Enabled token SIDs and restricting SIDs undergo two checks; both must allow the access.
WRITE_RESTRICTED applies restricting SIDs only to writes. Creating from an already restricted token intersects the restricting SID lists.
FILE_DELETE_CHILD is a directory-specific access right; checking only DELETE on the child is insufficient to explain an actual delete result.
AppContainer access is an intersection of user/group and package/capability grants, with low integrity; LPAC needs further explicit capabilities for otherwise common system resources.

safe_repair_route: Keep the elevated admission refusal in production until the same actual-child backend proves the original isolation invariants and positive functionality. A refusal test is not a passing execution test.

Use the existing native diagnostic harness to record the first failing system API, GetLastError, actual spawned-child token SID/restricted SID/integrity information, requested access and effective ACLs. Repair the narrow missing read/launch/IPC capability at that API boundary; do not guess based only on a synthetic AccessCheck.

One candidate architecture is a fully restricted capability token with explicit grants needed for system image/DLL reads, selected roots and authenticated IPC. A second is an AppContainer/LPAC process with an explicit resource capability list. Both remain unqualified here: dropping WRITE_RESTRICTED or successfully creating a token alone is not a complete repair.

For the selected architecture run the existing four-cell deletion matrix through a real production child and unchanged budgets, exercising the child DELETE and parent FILE_DELETE_CHILD routes independently for in-root permitted and out-of-root denied effects. Retain assertions on actual file existence/results, not just token masks or API setup.

Then preserve ordinary reads, process and DLL launch, root-scoped writes/deletes, authenticated broker/owner-local IPC, constrained network behavior, cancellation and cleanup. Keep all existing required CI failures visible until these pass.

The separate frozen dependency-lock digest mismatch can be repaired by regenerating canonical metadata for reviewed dependency changes, inspecting it, then updating exact frozen pins; this does not justify weakening ACL or source/test identity preflight predicates.
rejected_shortcuts: Removing or bypassing the admission guard before positive and negative native evidence
Changing original successful-execution tests to accept refusal or skipping Windows required jobs
Adding Everyone/logon broad granting SIDs to make launch or IPC pass
Rewriting arbitrary real parent-directory ACLs to hide FILE_DELETE_CHILD instead of isolating the child token
Treating a passing AccessCheck emulation, token creation, or standalone diagnostic as production backend qualification
